- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 3–7 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–8% if recent sentiment shifts from negative to neutral/bullish.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3-day smoothing or reduce forecast volatility by 15–25%.
- If sentiment is consistently bearish and price is falling, model often undercorrects; increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment remains negative but price is trending down.
